FGEN-CTX-G2.title: Riverbend Family Clinic - preparing for your annual physical
FGEN-CTX-G2.text:
RIVERBEND FAMILY CLINIC
Preparing for Your Annual Physical

Thank you for booking your annual physical with Riverbend Family Clinic. This sheet explains how to prepare so your visit runs smoothly. Your visit will be with Dr. Hollis Varga or a member of her care team.

Before your visit
- If your provider ordered fasting bloodwork (such as a lipid panel or fasting glucose), do not eat or drink anything except water for 10 hours before your appointment. Please avoid coffee, including black coffee, and chewing gum during the fasting period. Take your usual medications with water unless your provider has told you otherwise.
- Complete the health history questionnaire in the patient portal at least 2 days before your visit. If you cannot use the portal, arrive 30 minutes early to fill it in on paper.
- Make a list of every medication, vitamin and supplement you take, including the dose.

What to bring
- Photo ID and your current insurance card.
- Your medication list.
- Glasses or hearing aids if you use them.
- Any home blood pressure readings from the last month.

Arriving
Please arrive 15 minutes before your appointment time to check in. If you are more than 15 minutes late, we may need to reschedule you. Parking is available in Lot B behind the building; bring your ticket to the front desk for 2 hours of free validated parking. Street parking on Weller Avenue is metered.

During your visit
Your visit includes a review of your history, vital signs, a physical exam, and any screenings recommended for your age. Flu shots are available at no extra charge during your physical from October through March while supplies last. If you have a specific concern, mention it at check-in so enough time can be set aside; a separate appointment may be needed for complex issues.

After your visit
Lab results are posted to the patient portal, usually within 3 business days. Your provider will message you if anything needs follow-up. Normal results may be posted without a personal note. Follow-up visits can often be done by telehealth.

Cancellations
We ask for at least 24 hours notice if you need to cancel or reschedule. Appointments missed or cancelled with less than 24 hours notice are subject to a $40 missed-appointment fee, which is not covered by insurance.

Billing
Most insurance plans cover one preventive physical per year at no cost to you. Additional services discussed or treated during the visit, such as a new problem or a chronic condition review, may be billed separately and may involve a copay. Questions about coverage should be directed to your insurance company; our billing office can provide the procedure codes.

Front desk hours: Monday to Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.; Saturday, 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m.

Harbor Point Happenings - October Newsletter

Hello neighbors! Here is your quick roundup of what the board decided in September and what is coming up this month.

Elevator news
Good news for Building A: the board approved the controller replacement for the elevator, and we expect it back in service by October 30. Thank you for your patience with the stairs.

Pets
The board kept the limit at two pets per unit and removed the old weight limit for dogs, so bigger dogs are welcome. Every pet needs to be registered with the management office by November 1. Forms are at the front desk.

Guest parking
New hang-tag guest passes are on the way. Each unit gets two. Please keep them visible on your rear-view mirror.

Pool
The pool closes for the season on October 18. The pump timer has been adjusted after complaints about night noise.

Roof project
The board picked Kessler Roofing for the roof. More details at the next meeting.

Reminders from the management office
Moving in or out? The Building A elevator will be out until early December, so please book the freight stairs slot and plan extra help. FGEN-CTX-G1.title: Maple Court Apartments - resident notice, fall building works
FGEN-CTX-G1.text:
MAPLE COURT APARTMENTS - RESIDENT NOTICE
Issued September 28, 2026 by the Management Office, 410 Alder Street

Dear residents,

This notice covers building work planned for October and November, plus a few reminders about payments and common areas. Please keep it for reference.

1. Water shutoff
The water supply to all units will be shut off on Wednesday, October 14, from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. while the plumbing contractor replaces the main riser valve on the ground floor. Please fill containers the night before if you need water during that window. When service returns, run your cold tap for two to three minutes to clear any discoloured water. If water has not returned by 2:00 p.m., call the office.

2. Elevator modernization
The passenger elevator will be out of service from Monday, October 19 through Friday, November 6 while the cab, controls and doors are replaced. The freight elevator is not available to residents during this period. Residents who need mobility assistance during the elevator work should contact the office by October 9 so we can arrange help with groceries and deliveries. Large deliveries and move-ins will not be scheduled during these three weeks.

3. Parking permits
Annual parking permits expire on October 31. Renewal costs $45 per vehicle and can be completed through the resident portal or at the office. Vehicles without a current permit after November 7 may be towed at the owner's expense. Guest parking is limited to 48 hours per visit; guests must display a paper pass available from the office.

4. Rent payments
Rent is due on the 1st of each month. A late fee of $75 applies if rent has not been received by the end of the 5th. Payments through the resident portal by bank transfer (ACH) have no processing fee. Card payments are accepted but carry a 2.5% processing fee charged by the payment provider. Cash is not accepted at the office.

5. Package room
The package room on the lobby level is open from 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. daily. Packages not collected within 10 days will be returned to the carrier. Perishable deliveries should be picked up the same day.

6. Pest inspection
Our pest control vendor will carry out a routine inspection of all kitchens and bathrooms on Tuesday, October 27, between 8:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. You do not need to be home. Please clear the area under your kitchen sink.

7. Quiet hours and common areas
Quiet hours are 10:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m. The rooftop terrace closes for the season on November 1. The bike storage room is currently full; ask the office to join the waitlist.

8. Lease renewals
Residents whose leases end in the coming months will receive a renewal offer at least 60 days before the lease end date. If you have not received yours by then, please contact the office.

Office hours are Monday to Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. The property manager is Dana Okafor. For after-hours emergencies such as flooding or no heat, call the emergency line listed on the back of your unit door.

Thank you for your patience while we complete these improvements.

Maple Court Management Office

items.question: I'm trying to decide between leasing a new car and buying a used one. I drive about 8,000 miles a year, I have about 6,000 saved, and I really hate dealing with repairs. Walk me through the trade-offs and tell me which way you'd lean.
items.answer:
At 8,000 miles a year you're driving well under the average, which is the single biggest factor here. Leasing usually wins on the repair side, since you're covered by warranty for the whole term and you hand the car back before anything major wears out. The catch is that low mileage doesn't lower your payment much, and you're paying for depreciation you'll never own.

Buying used flips that. You own an asset at the end, insurance and registration are typically cheaper, and you're not locked into mileage caps. But you're exposed to repairs once the warranty runs out, which is exactly what you said you hate.

With 6,000 saved, I'd lean toward a used car that's still under its factory warranty, ideally a certified pre-owned one. You get the ownership and lower long-term cost, plus a warranty cushion so repairs aren't your problem for a while. If the monthly payment matters more than owning anything, leasing is the cleaner fit.
